chapter: Long Island years and Battle's estate
title: Brother Roosevelt's piano records
summary: Roosevelt recorded originals on a bad piano for Battle, singing and playing like Fats Waller, and the records never came out.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: These records, these groups that Battle recorded, they never came out, huh?
No, fool around with the records too long. He'd fool around. Got a lot of records on my brother and a lot of original songs. He sings and plays like Fats Waller, commercial tunes.
Which brother is that?
The one that died, the piano player.
And that was again?
Roosevelt.
Oh, Roosevelt.
Yeah, so he's got a lot of songs now, like to put them out, because he did them on the piano and Battles wants to dub around them, but he never gets to the point --
No, that's what I think.
-- and I heard those records are good, but he made the records.
Yeah.
But he made them on his piano, bad piano. So, he loved that old sound. He thought that was something great. He had an idea that that old piano was the thing, but that wasn't it.
Well, that's all right, if you're
going to put them out yourself, but when you go to sell them, immediately say the piano's out of tune or something.
See, but he played so much piano until he could make a piano sound like it wasn't there, see?
Oh, yeah?

But that wasn't justice to him, because he could do things (inaudible) never know the piano was was . Jim Evans always asked me, say, "I don't know music, but is he playing as much piano as you think he is or is he jiving -- or is he really playing that much piano?" He was playing.

Because when he played on the road, Winonie (inaudible) had to let him go because when he play, everybody come all up on the stage and get around him.
Well, he sang on all of them, did he?
Yeah, all them tunes (inaudible) he sung.
But he didn't make any solos?
Yeah, solos and sing. He had a lot of tunes like "You Know What I Mean When I Say That I Mean I Love You," and things like Fats Waller.
Yeah, yeah.
But they was not like Fats, just other

things and then some of the things was great. I got three or four of the sheets now and I got those tapes, whenever I got a chance to go there, I'll get them, you know? Maybe I could do something with them.
You don't know. You could --

Yeah, but when he was fixing to do things with those records for so long.
Yeah.
You know?
I don't think he knew the difference between a good record and a bad record. I mean, you know --
Well, you know, the production of them was not good. I mean, the sound of them --
